title: MigrationState
$comment: Dual-build state manager: the resumable, per-unit-reversible record. The agent updates it after every unit; tools/state.py validates it.

judge_validation.$comment: Stage 2 hard gate: judge-first results before any translation

rust_module.$comment: importable rust module when the wheel layout is NOT per-unit: the flat PyO3 extension module (e.g. wicksmith_core) exposing every unit's functions; state.py shim prefers this over deriving from rust_path (issue #53)

rust_names.$comment: the unit's exported public names in the rust module — one source of truth shared by the shim's re-export list and the reviewer's API-freeze check; presence (non-empty) selects flat-wheel shim mode (issue #53)

status.$comment: ported/escalated etc. always keep python fallback until 'retired' in Stage 7

notes.$comment: per-unit audit trail; prose for humans (tools/glv-subagents.md)

sessions.$comment: per-unit session audit trail when delegates run as GLV sessions; the orchestrator, never a delegate, writes these

gate.$comment: scope_change = MIGRATION_PROMPT.md mandatory gate 'any scope change later'; no_equivalent_dependency is resolved by policy DEP-1 (descope, never a substitution)

state.$comment: deferred = resolved by policy as defer-not-halt (ESC-1); a resolved gate is never blocking

decided_by.$comment: 'human' or 'policy:<rule-id>' referencing autonomy/policy.json (state.py checks the pattern and the rule id); required on any non-open gate

policy_version.$comment: the autonomy/policy.json version the rule was evaluated against (required when decided_by starts with policy:)

evidence.$comment: key=value measurement records the policy evaluated (or the human reviewed): spike_verdict=, bench_improvement_pct=, shadow_diff_rate=, shadow_samples=, canary_green_minutes=, rollback_tested=, module=, python= — extracted, never invented

autonomy.$comment: Pre-authorized autonomy for this run (issue #22). Set once BEFORE the run starts (state.py init --autonomy-level / pipeline.py run --autonomy) and journaled on change; the driver enforces it, the agent cannot raise it mid-run. There are zero mid-run questions at L2+.

level.$comment: L0 supervised (hard stops: the gate stays open, the run ends with the dossier — the operator decides between runs, nothing asks mid-run) · L1 agent proposes into the dossier, operator decides between runs · L2 all gates policy-resolved (the default), publish disabled · L3 full autopilot incl. cutover

policy_version.$comment: autonomy/policy.json version in force for this run

budget.$comment: run-level ceilings enforced by tools/pipeline.py; over either ceiling the run ends in the budget_exhausted terminal state

max_chain_depth.$comment: issue #25 — the successor-session chain cap: session-level budget_exhausted spawns a successor GLV session automatically (tools/succession.py); this is how many successions may chain before the run ends failed_safely. The run-level ceilings above bound the whole chain (sum over sessions); successors get a fresh session budget, never a fresh run budget. Policy default 10.

publish_allowed.$comment: must be true (L3 only) for a policy-approved cutover; state.py rejects the combination otherwise

preflight.$comment: Issue #31 — one command (tools/pipeline.py preflight) runs and records everything stages 0/3 silently assumed: target suite green + wall time (the Stage 2 spec baseline), pytest collection capture, the oracle.py self-test re-proven per run, rust-template reachability + HEAD SHA (Stage 3 provenance), cargo/rustc/maturin/uv + gate-stack presence, the target venv/interpreter/Py_GIL_DISABLED wheel flavor/derived PYO3_PYTHON, substitutions.json freshness, and framework-vs-target interpreter match. Hard prerequisites failing leaves ok=false with hard_failures[] — later stages must not assume what preflight could not prove.

ok.$comment: false when any hard prerequisite (suite green, oracle self-test 5/5, rust-template reachable) failed or could not run

framework_python.$comment: the interpreter running the framework tools

hard_failures.$comment: check ids that failed: suite / oracle_selftest / template

target.$comment: machine-facing summary Stage 3/4 pin from; root is recorded so preflight re-runs need no --target-root

root.$comment: absolute path of the repo being migrated

pyo3_python.$comment: derived PYO3_PYTHON for maturin/justfile dev-build pins

checks.$comment: full per-check records keyed by id: template, oracle_selftest, pytest_collect, suite, toolchain, target_interpreter, substitutions_freshness, interpreter_match — each with ok/skipped/detail plus its raw evidence (head_sha, counts, wall_seconds, versions, paths, tails); deliberately free-form so a check can grow evidence without a schema change

run_status.$comment: Terminal-state discipline (issue #22): a driver run ALWAYS ends in complete / no_go_measured / budget_exhausted / failed_safely — never 'awaiting input'. Every terminal state emits the same deliverable set (run report incl. the escalation dossier, state file, journal). Issue #25: session-level budget_exhausted never survives a successor chain — tools/succession.py spawns the successor automatically over the GLV transport it bootstraps itself (issue #47); budget_exhausted remains a final status only for the run-level ceilings.

session_chain.$comment: Issue #25 — the successor-session chain record, written by tools/succession.py through state.py's validated writer. budget_exhausted at the SESSION level (the orchestrator's context window) is a scheduling event: the harness spawns a successor GLV session with full resume context, journals a stop-notice (operator informed, not involved), and resets run_status to running. Guardrails recorded here: depth cap + per-session progress snapshots powering the monotonic-progress guard (a successor that advances neither stage nor ≥1 decided unit terminates the chain failed_safely — no infinite resume loops). Run-level ceilings (autonomy.budget) bound the entire chain; token spend sums through this one state file.

depth.$comment: successions so far = sessions - 1 (session 1 is the operator's prompt, not a succession)

max_depth.$comment: the cap in force for this chain; over it the run ends failed_safely with the dossier

wall_clock_minutes.$comment: run-level wall clock summed over every session in the chain (each session adds settled_at - started_at)

sessions.$comment: orchestrator sessions, contiguous from index 1, oldest first; named run-<project>-s<n> per tools/glv-subagents.md

name.$comment: run-<project>-s<index> — the succession surfaces in GLV session listings

glv_status.$comment: GLV run-status vocabulary: queued | running | completed | stopped | error | idle

outcome.$comment: the run_status the session left in the state file

succession_reason.$comment: why this session was spawned (null for session 1: the operator's single prompt)

progress_snapshot.$comment: observable state at this session's spawn — the bar the session must clear for the chain to continue

notices.$comment: stop-notices: one per succession (and any transport failure that ends the chain) — the operator-informing artifact; the operator stays informed, not involved

journal.$comment: append-only transition log; every state.py write appends one entry — 'every state transition journaled' (tools/README.md #4)

unit.$comment: unit id, or null for project-level fields (e.g. stage)

field.$comment: dotted path to the changed field, e.g. stage or units[u3].status

from.$comment: any JSON value; null = previously unset

to.$comment: any JSON value; null = now unset

actor.$comment: who made the transition: orchestrator, state.py, or a GLV session id

budget_ledger.$comment: running totals vs the Stage 0 projection; deviations reported in the end-of-run report (and reviewed by the operator between runs)
